title: LR vs. SVM & the SGDClassifier
keyPoints: Large data or need probabilities → logistic regression; clear margin on little data → SVM.
SGDClassifier proves the insight: LR and SVM are the same model — only the loss differs (log vs. hinge).
Scale features before SVMs, and use a Pipeline to prevent leakage.

blocks.html: Both are linear classifiers and both can use kernels. Sharpest difference: in logistic regression all points influence the fit, in an SVM only the support vectors. And by convention “SVM” means: hinge loss plus L2 regularization.

rows: common — fast with few support vectors

blocks.html: Fitting a linear SVM can also be done via SVC(kernel='linear'), but LinearSVC is often faster. And there are more hyperparameters than these — dare to read the documentation.

sections.title: SGDClassifier: proof that only the loss differs

blocks.html: SGDClassifier handles larger datasets and switches between LR and SVM via the loss hyperparameter alone — the model is the same. Gotcha: regularization is called alpha here (the inverse of C: higher = more regularization).

blocks.caption: Two lines to switch between LR and a linear SVM
blocks.source:
from sklearn.datasets import load_wine
from sklearn.linear_model import SGDClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

X, y = load_wine(return_X_y=True)
X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=42)
scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_tr)
X_tr, X_te = scaler.transform(X_tr), scaler.transform(X_te)

for loss, label in [('hinge', 'linear SVM'), ('log_loss', 'logistic regression')]:
    sgd = SGDClassifier(loss=loss, max_iter=2000, tol=1e-3, random_state=42)
    sgd.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
    print(f'loss={loss:<9} ({label})  train={sgd.score(X_tr, y_tr):.3f}'
          f'  test={sgd.score(X_te, y_te):.3f}')

blocks.html: Linear classifiers share one prediction step (the sign of \( w \cdot x + b \)); what distinguishes them is the loss optimised during fitting — logistic loss, hinge loss, or something else.

sections.title: Where does all of this fit in the bigger picture?

blocks.html: Zoom out: data science spans everything from data collection to communication; ML is a branch within it, supervised learning within that, classification within that — and LR and SVMs within that. Next on this site: tree-based methods and calculus.
